chapters.title: EventScope — follow the event, keep the evidence.
chapters.caption: A prediction-market research desk for people who need to cite what they actually observed.

chapters.title: A quote needs context.
chapters.caption: The market, phase, observation time and missing-data limits matter alongside the percentage.

chapters.title: Discover with purpose.
chapters.caption: Panta categories and market phases power the filters. Text search covers only loaded catalogue pages.

chapters.title: Detail reads supply the quotes.
chapters.caption: YES and NO retain the API values. Catalogue volume is not claimed as 24-hour volume.

chapters.title: Watch a small set of events.
chapters.caption: Up to four watched events refresh every 30 seconds while this browser is open. History stays local.

chapters.title: Compare observations, not invented relationships.
chapters.caption: Each event keeps its own timestamp and resolution condition. Side-by-side quotes do not prove correlation.

chapters.title: Observation history starts when you observe.
chapters.caption: These are actual reads of the fictional feed during this recording. No earlier history is preloaded.

chapters.title: Alerts wait for adequate evidence.
chapters.caption: A valid 10–15-minute baseline is required. Missing quotes, phase switches, stale reads and long gaps pause signals.

chapters.title: Freeze one reproducible research capture.
chapters.caption: The brief fixes the market, source mode, quotes and original read timestamp. Later reads cannot silently replace it.

chapters.title: Carry the data limits with the evidence.
chapters.caption: A brief reports missing baselines and bounded trade records. It invents no news explanation or causal attribution.

chapters.title: Export the same capture in three formats.
chapters.caption: Markdown for writing, JSON for structured research, CSV for spreadsheets — all explicitly preserve the example mode.

chapters.title: Trade records have their own boundary.
chapters.caption: Share amounts are not trade notional. Fictional records have no explorer links; valid live signatures can link out.

chapters.title: Missing remains missing.
chapters.caption: Unavailable quotes never become zero. Readable market conditions remain available without a fabricated chart.

chapters.title: Source interpretation is part of the product.
chapters.caption: API read time is not the last on-chain trade or Panta’s internal update time. The interface explains this distinction.

chapters.title: Four Panta read resources form the core workflow.
chapters.caption: Categories, catalogue, detail quotes and trades. Credentials stay on the server; no wallet or transactions are needed.

chapters.title: Independent prototype. Honest delivery status.
chapters.caption: Production API checks and real observations are documented separately. This video uses examples; competition entries remain pending.
